premise: Interesting people are not born with better stories. They have simply said yes to more things, gone further, and stayed longer than was comfortable. This campaign is about accumulating a life that is worth describing — and then being someone who can describe it.

reps.label: Did something for the first time
reps.hint: Anything. First times are the raw material.

reps.label: Said yes to something
reps.hint: Especially the invitation you would normally decline.

reps.label: Went somewhere new
reps.hint: A street, a district, a town. New is new.

reps.label: It was a waste of time
reps.hint: Some of them are. That is the price of the ones that are not.

reps.label: Told someone about it
reps.hint: An experience nobody hears about is only half spent.

principles.title: You are running a loop
principles.body: Most weeks are copies. Same rooms, same route, same six meals, same four people. Nothing is wrong with any of it except that a copied week leaves nothing behind — which is why the last two years feel shorter than they were.

principles.title: Novelty is what makes time feel long
principles.body: Unfamiliar days are encoded in more detail, so they read as longer in memory. A month of routine compresses into nothing; a week of new places feels substantial for years. If you want a longer life, this is the lever you actually control.

principles.title: Default yes, for a while
principles.body: Your no is automatic and it is not really a decision. Suspend it. Say yes to things you would normally decline and let the results, rather than your reflex, tell you what you like. You can go back to filtering once you have data.

principles.title: Most of it will be mediocre
principles.body: A good proportion of what you try will be dull, awkward or a waste of an afternoon. This is not a sign the strategy is failing — it is the cost structure. You cannot get the standout experiences without buying the ordinary ones too.

principles.title: Go alone sometimes
principles.body: Waiting for company is the most common reason people do not go. Going alone removes the scheduling problem entirely, and it changes the experience: you notice more, meet more people, and stop performing for whoever came with you.

principles.title: Depth is also interesting
principles.body: Endless novelty becomes its own kind of shallow. The person who has been to forty countries briefly is often less interesting than the one who knows one thing properly. Alternate breadth with going deep on something.

principles.title: Tell it well
principles.body: An experience nobody hears about is only half spent. Being interesting is partly a storytelling skill: what you leave out, where you start, being willing to be the fool in your own account. Practise it deliberately.

principles.title: Become the person who organises it
principles.body: There is a step past having an interesting life: making other people's lives more interesting. The person who proposes the trip and books it ends up at the centre of everything, permanently.

missions.do: Write down what you did last week. All of it. Then read it back.
missions.why: The loop is invisible until it is on paper. Look at it before changing it.

missions.do: Change one fixed thing about your day today.
missions.why: Route, meal, hour, seat. Prove the fixed things are not fixed.

missions.do: Say yes to the next invitation, whatever it is.
missions.why: Do not evaluate it. That is the mission — the evaluation is the loop talking.

missions.do: Go somewhere in your own town you have never been.
missions.why: The unexplored is closer than you think. Usually two streets away.

missions.do: Do something on your own that you would normally need company for.
missions.why: Waiting for company is why most things never happen. Remove the dependency.

missions.do: Try something with a real chance of being terrible.
missions.why: The bad ones are the entry fee for the good ones. Buy one deliberately.

missions.do: Spend an evening with no plan and no phone map.
missions.why: Structure is comfortable and it prevents anything unscheduled from happening.

missions.do: Ask someone what the most interesting thing they did this year was. Then do a version of it.
missions.why: Other people's lives are the cheapest source of ideas available to you.

missions.do: Go to an event for something you know nothing about.
missions.why: A talk, a match, a show, a service. Be a beginner in public for an hour.

missions.do: Say yes to three things this week without checking whether you feel like it.
missions.why: Volume week. Your feelings are a lagging indicator, not a planning tool.

missions.do: Take a whole day somewhere you have never spent a day.
missions.why: A day is different from a visit. Stay long enough to get bored and past it.

missions.do: Learn one thing well enough to show someone this week.
missions.why: Collecting experiences is half of it. Collecting capabilities is the other half.

missions.do: Do the thing you have described as 'not really me'.
missions.why: That phrase is a wall you built without checking what was on the other side.

missions.do: Go somewhere at an hour you never go — dawn, or late.
missions.why: The same place runs different lives at different hours. Go see another one.

missions.do: Travel somewhere overnight, alone.
missions.why: Waking somewhere unfamiliar with nobody to consult is the core of this campaign.

missions.do: Tell someone about something you did recently. Properly, as a story.
missions.why: Where you start, what you leave out, being the fool in it. Practise the telling.

missions.do: Follow up on something you tried and liked. Do it a second time.
missions.why: Novelty is a search process. When it finds something, stop searching and dig.

missions.do: Meet someone whose life looks nothing like yours.
missions.why: Your sense of what is possible is capped by who you know. Raise the cap.

missions.do: Do something that will be a story in ten years.
missions.why: You know the difference between a nice afternoon and a story. Go get one.

missions.do: Spend a weekend on one thing, properly, rather than three things briefly.
missions.why: Depth. Forty shallow experiences are less interesting than one real one.

missions.do: Organise something for other people and see it through.
missions.why: Move from attending to convening. Everything changes at this step.

missions.do: Go somewhere that needs actual planning to reach.
missions.why: The friction filters out most people, which is exactly why it is worth doing.

missions.do: Do something slightly beyond what you are ready for.
missions.why: Competence arrives during the attempt. It has never once arrived beforehand.

missions.do: Take someone with you who would never have gone alone.
missions.why: Being the reason someone else's life got bigger is the top of this ladder.

missions.do: Say yes to the thing that scares you slightly.
missions.why: Not danger. The one where you might look stupid. That is the correct dose.

missions.do: Spend a week where every single day contains something you have never done.
missions.why: Seven consecutive firsts. It is harder and more interesting than it sounds.

missions.do: Book the trip you have been describing for years.
missions.why: Describing it has been a substitute for going. Pay for it today.

missions.do: Build the thing you keep wishing existed near you.
missions.why: The club, the night, the group. Someone has to start it and nobody has.

missions.do: Write down what you did in the last thirty days. Compare it to step one.
missions.why: This is the proof. Two lists, same person, thirty days apart.

missions.do: Commit to the biggest thing on your list, with a date and money down.
missions.why: You have spent thirty steps proving the loop was optional. Now spend it on something large.
